scientific_question: Does stage-by-stage residual refitting under the Frobenius control's angle trust radius turn the consistent but weak task-aware pair-selection gain into a cross-window stable output32 update?

identity.execution_commit_rule: record a clean pushed commit containing this immutable plan before implementation

shared_chart.feedback: zero for this one-step prospective diagnostic
shared_chart.weight_decay_application: identical production ordering in all arms

arms.frobenius_simultaneous: Existing output32 control: Frobenius-selected pairs and all diagonal angles fitted at the same pre-output source and residual.
arms.frobenius_sequential_trust: Reuse the Frobenius control's fixed 32 matchings, but before each stage refit that stage's Frobenius angle on current source and remaining residual, clamp by the per-cell trust radius, apply it, and subtract the realized update.
arms.task_gradient_sequential_trust: Reuse the preregistered RMS-normalized residual-plus-fit-task-gradient fixed 32 matchings, then use the identical sequential Frobenius refit and trust clamp.

trust_radius.definition: For each layer-phase cell, max_abs(diagonal_metric_angles(S,R,frobenius_control_pairs)) from the existing simultaneous Frobenius output32 control.
trust_radius.application: Clamp every sequentially refitted scalar angle in both sequential arms to [-radius,+radius].

prohibited: selection on holdout gradient or activations

pass_all: all arms use exactly 147456 coordinates per selected layer
all sequential angles obey the shared per-cell trust radius
aggregate held-out predicted CE descent is positive and strictly greater than frobenius_sequential_trust
fit and holdout task-descent advantages over frobenius_sequential_trust are positive with holdout/fit retention >=0.10
aggregate held-out activation-output residual energy is no more than 1.10 times frobenius_sequential_trust
aggregate update energy is no more than 1.10 times frobenius_sequential_trust
task candidate beats frobenius_sequential_trust on all 4 held-out finite-step CE comparisons and at least 7 of all 8 comparisons
mean task-candidate finite-step CE is at least 0.0005 lower than frobenius_sequential_trust
mean task-candidate finite-step CE is no worse than the existing frobenius_simultaneous control
decision_rule.pass_action: preregister the exact production selector and sequential refit, add correctness tests, require an I/O-inclusive >=20% MFU preflight, then consider exactly one 124M causal run
decision_rule.fail_action: reject current output32 task-gradient chart and return to a cross-batch consensus direction or different structured MLP parameterization; no causal training
